Two asks from our side:
- How will those calls be metered against the negotiated minimum in our draft SOW? Is the minimum applied per-session, per-invoice, or per distinct call?
- How do you round partial-token usage for these long calls (e.g., do you round the whole request up to the nearest 1k tokens, or round independently for prompt/completion)?

We want to avoid surprises on our first invoice — can you show a few worked examples based on the attached CSV? Also attaching procurement on this thread so they have visibility.

Quick notes up front:

- Metering logic depends on the SKU you're on. For the hybrid long-context SKU we suggested, metering is done per request: prompt tokens and completion tokens are counted, some prefix/cache reuse is accounted for separately. Rounding rules are applied at the invoice-line level per request grouping.

Hi Sarah — I pulled three representative rows from your CSV and did line-by-line math. Summary first, full workbook attached.

Summary rules we use for the SKU in your SOW (hybrid-longcontext-v2):
1) Metering unit: per-call token accounting. Each call = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens + any delta for extra KV fetches.
2) Rounding: we round each call's total token count up to the nearest 100 tokens for metering. (Rationale: reduces invoice line noise for micro-variations.)
3) Minimums: the monthly committed minimum is applied at invoice aggregation. If sum(metered_tokens_per_month) < committed_tokens, invoice is for committed_tokens. Overage is per-token at agreed rate.
4) Cache reuse: if a prompt prefix is cached and reused across N calls within the same session, we charge the full tokens for the first call and 25% of that prefix for subsequent calls when prefix is identical — this approximates KV amortization in practice.

Worked examples (pulled from your sample):
A) Short triage call
- prompt: 320 tokens; completion: 180 tokens; raw total = 500 => rounded up to 500 (already multiple of 100)
- metered tokens = 500
B) Long transcript summarize (example you described)
- prompt (transcript): 12,340 tokens; completion: 210 tokens; raw total = 12,550 => rounded up to 12,600
- metered tokens = 12,600
C) Multi-call session with prefix reuse (3 calls share a 6k-token prefix; first call has full prefix, subsequent calls charge 25% of prefix)
- call1: prompt 6,200 + completion 500 => raw 6,700 => rounded 6,700
- call2: prompt 25%*6,200=1,550 + completion 300 => raw 1,850 => rounded 1,900
- call3: prompt 25%*6,200=1,550 + completion 450 => raw 2,000 => rounded 2,000
- session metered tokens = 6,700 + 1,900 + 2,000 = 10,600

Invoice mapping notes:
- We export per-request metered units and then aggregate per invoice line. Your invoice will show both metered_units and committed_credit_applied.
- Example: If committed_tokens per month is 50,000 and your metered_tokens are 38,150, we'll invoice 50,000 (committed); your overage column will be zero. If you hit 52,300, invoice = 50,000 + 2,300 at overage price.

Edge cases:
- Streams that keep open sockets with heartbeats: heartbeats are ignored for token metering unless there is actual token exchange.
- Partial-token rounding anti-abuse: if a single call is artificially split into many tiny calls to inflate rounding, we run a post-process that buckets sequential calls within a 2s window and applies call-level coalescing for metering (rare).

I've attached the workbook with line-by-line math for the three examples. Happy to hop on a 25-min call to step through.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Finance, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that is very helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement:
- Can you confirm how that committed monthly minimum reads against our milestone billing? Our legal team prefers commitment recognition on a calendar-month basis but wants to be sure an initial ramp (month 1) won't surprise them.
- For the prefix amortization rule (25% subsequent calls), can you confirm whether that applies across sessions when the same prefix is reused (our workload sometimes reconstructs the same prefix after short gaps)?

Procurement would also like a worked invoice sample that shows: billed_units, committed_credit_applied, overage_units, and effective unit price after discount for this deal. If you can include that as a one-page PDF in the SOW package we can fast-track internal approval.

Best,

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

1) Committed minimum vs milestone billing: we will treat the committed token spend on a calendar-month basis. For Month 1 ramp, we can offer a one-time pro-rata concession so your legal team doesn't see an unexpected full-month commit on the first invoice. (We will document this concession in the SOW.)

2) Prefix amortization across sessions: amortization applies when the backend KV/prefix is materially identical and reused within our cache TTL (currently 72 hours). If your workload reconstructs the identical prefix within that TTL and the model-server records reuse, the 25% amortization will apply on subsequent requests across sessions. If it is re-ingested differently we cannot assume reuse. We'll add language to the SOW that clarifies TTL and evidence requirements (server logs) for cross-session amortization claims.

3) Invoice sample: Ben will produce a one-page PDF example that maps metered_units -> committed_credit_applied -> overage_units and shows the discounted effective price. We'll attach that to the SOW package.

Proposed next steps (MAP):
- Mon 09 Jun: Ben to deliver the one-page invoice sample PDF and an updated SOW excerpt reflecting pro-rata Month 1 concession.
- Tue 10 Jun: 25-min call (Marissa + Ben + Vanessa + Sarah + procurement) to walk the invoice example.
- Wed 11 Jun: Clearwave to confirm signature decision or ask for a single redline.

If that timeline works I'll update the SOW and send a DocuSign link for the v1 SOW with the concession noted.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Marissa Cole
